extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of prescriptive and argumentative passages from a chapter of Rabelais' Pantagruel discussing marriage, cuckoldry, and remedies for concupiscence; the page is a prose-satirical treatment mixing anecdotes, counsel, and learned references. Useful for literary analysis or extracting period advice/argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-judgment in marriage decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyone in the project and enterprise of marriage ought to be his own carver, sole arbitrator of his proper thoughts, and from himself alone take counsel in the main and peremptory closure of what his determination should be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pantagruel advises that the prospective spouse should decide for himself rather than delegating the ultimate decision to others; the passage emphasizes personal responsibility in the marriage choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware philauty (self-love) bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Philauty, or self-love, is that which blinds your judgment and deceiveth you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text warns that self-love can distort judgement in matrimonial decisions; readers are urged to recognize this bias when weighing counsel or desires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult appropriate experts for each concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever we are, or have, consisteth in three things—the soul, the body, and the goods. Now, for the preservation of these three, there are three sorts of learned men ordained, each respectively to have care of that one which is recommended to his charge: theologues for the soul, physicians for the welfare of the body, and lawyers for the safety of our goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical counsel: consult a theologian about spiritual matters, a physician about bodily concerns, and a lawyer about property/contractual aspects of marriage; Pantagruel assembles such a panel (plus a philosopher) to advise Panurge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marry if you lack continency (practical marital counsel)
rubrics_metrics.description: If thou hast not obtained from God the gift and special grace of continency, my counsel to you in that case is that you marry; for you should rather choose to marry once than to burn still in fires of concupiscence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hippothadee (the theologue) gives the prescriptive criterion: when one cannot keep sexual continence, marriage is the advised remedy to avoid ongoing sexual torment; framed as moral-theological counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a wife of commendable extraction and piety to avoid cuckoldry
rubrics_metrics.description: You shall never be a cuckold... if you make choice of one of a commendable extraction, descended of honest parents, and instructed in all piety and virtue—such a one as hath not at any time haunted or frequented the company or conversation of those that are of corrupt and depraved manners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hippothadee argues that selecting a virtuous, pious, well-bred woman who fears God and has good upbringing is the canonical way to prevent adultery; the passage includes social/religious criteria (parentage, piety, instruction) as safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead by virtuous example to encourage wife's fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Your behaviour is to be such, that you are to go before her in a good example, by entertaining her unfeignedly with a conjugal amity, by continually approving yourself in all your words and actions a faithful and discreet husband... and by living, not only at home and privately with your own household and family, but in the face also of all men and open view of the world, devoutly, virtuously, and chastely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The husband must model the behaviour he expects: public and private piety and conjugal fidelity are prescribed as ways to cultivate the wife's adherence to marital vows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hans Carvel ring (talismanic/detection anecdote)
rubrics_metrics.description: The devil gave Hans Carvel a ring, saying, 'whilst thou carriest it upon that finger, thy wife shall never carnally be known by any other than thyself without thy special knowledge and consent.' Hans Carvel declared he would never take it off; the anecdote ends with the middle finger found inside the wife's body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an 'infallible and sovereign antidote' in the tale, this is a satirical, talismanic 'remedy' for cuckoldry. The story functions as comic cautionary material rather than practical, but it exemplifies folkloric/absurd preventative measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abate lust by immoderate wine
rubrics_metrics.description: Wine abateth lust when immoderately taken; by intemperancy proceeding from the excessive drinking of strong liquor there is brought... a chillness in the blood...a numbness and hebetation of the senses—all which are great lets and impediments to the act of generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rondibilis (the physician) lists immoderate drinking as a medical means to cool sexual desire, while noting moderate drinking can increase desire; the guidance includes physiological explanations and classical testimonies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certain drugs, plants, and herbs to reduce sexual potency
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain drugs, plants, herbs, and roots... make the taker cold, maleficiated, unfit for, and unable to perform the act of generation; examples: water-lily, agnus castus, willow-twigs, hemp-stalks, woodbine, honeysuckle, tamarisk, chaste tree, mandrake, bennet, keckbugloss, the skin of a hippopotam, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physiomedical recommendation: specific ingredients (listed) can be dosed according to constitution to mortify or benumb the seminal capacity; Rondibilis also notes there are opposite ingredients that increase potency, and dosing must match the patient's humours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent physical labour to subdue lechery
rubrics_metrics.description: The ardour of lechery is very much subdued and mated by frequent labour and continual toiling... painful exercises and laborious working... bring upon the whole body such a dissolution... that there is neither time... nor power to afford the seminal resudation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical exertion and constant work are presented as prophylactic: idleness breeds lust, while active labor dissipates the bodily conditions needed for strong sexual appetite (classical and Hippocratic authority cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eager study and intellectual occupation blunt sexual desire
rubrics_metrics.description: The tickling pricks of incontinency are blunted by an eager study; in such a studiously musing person you shall see how all the arteries of his brains are stretched forth... so that all his natural faculties for that time will seem to be suspended from each their proper charge and office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rational/intellectual immersion (study, philosophy, arts) is given as a method to divert spirits from bodily passions; classical examples (Muses, philosophers) are used to illustrate chastity preserved by occupation of the mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent reiteration of sexual act (maceration) to tame the flesh
rubrics_metrics.description: By the too frequent reiteration of the act of venery... maceration and taming of the flesh... the hermits of Thebaide can no more aptly or expediently macerate and bring down the pride of their bodies... than by duffling and fanfreluching it five-and-twenty or thirty times a day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Another medical/ascetic recommendation: habitual, frequent intercourse reduces erotic excess through repeated exhaustion; the passage frames this as a traditional remedy ('maceration') recommended by some authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cuckoldry naturally attends marriage; vigilance recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no married man who doth not run the hazard of being made a cuckold. Cuckoldry naturally attendeth marriage... do not fail... to pry into her ways, and to espy what places she shall go to with her mother, and who those be that shall repair unto her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rondibilis and anecdotal Hippocratic counsel assert cuckoldry is a common accompaniment of marriage and recommends vigilance—avoiding leaving the wife in solitude and monitoring her company—as a practical precaution (presented as experienced observation).
